title: The Influence of Prolonged Therapeutic Fasting on Diabetic Fatty Liver and Muscle Build-up - an Exploratory Randomized Clinical Trial
summary: This study explores whether prolonged outpatient fasting is feasible for people with type 2 diabetes and provides an initial assessment of its effects on metabolism and fatty liver disease. It will also examine how fasting affects blood clotting tendency, body temperature, and muscle gain during physical activity. Three different fasting approaches will be compared: 14 days of water fasting, two 7-day periods of Buchinger-style juice fasting, and two 7-day periods of a fasting-mimicking diet (FMD). In addition, the study will investigate whether combining fasting with resistance training has beneficial effects on metabolic control in people with type 2 diabetes. The StudyU app, which is still under development, will be used to support participants during the study and may be adapted as needed.
conditions: Fatty (change of) liver, not elsewhere classified

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Presence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (≥ last 3 months no change in therapy) 
- HbA1c ≥ 6.5% without medication or 6.0% with medication 
- Sonographically suspected fatty liver disease or existing MRI evidence of fatty liver disease 
- Written informed consent form available
Exclusion criteria:
- Intensified insulin therapy 
- No sufficient verbal communication possible 
- Dementia or other severely cognitively impairing disease
- Current pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Other serious medical, neurological or psychiatric conditions
- History of gout
- History of gallstones / diagnosis of cholecystolithiasis
- Participation in another study
- Potential difficulties with the MRI scan, e.g. claustrophobia, pacemaker, electronic or magnetically responsive implants, permanent make-up, tattoos
